newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Solana, Primakov press on with Russia-NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: Solana, Primakov press on with Russia-NATO talks.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana held an unscheduled second day of talks on Wednesday to try to finalise a partnership pact between Moscow and the Western alliance.

The two officials agreed to resume talks after spending six hours on Tuesday trying to resolve differences over the document, intended to forge a peaceful relationship into the next century and address Russian fears over NATO expansion.
Solana arrived by car and said nothing to reporters as he entered the foreign minstry mansion where the talks are being held in central Moscow.
Russian officials also declined to comment on the progress of the talks, which they say will decide whether differences can be narrowed in time to sign the agreement in Paris on May 27.
Interfax news agency said a statement was expected when the negotiations ended.
President Boris Yeltsin says he wants to sign an agreement with NATO on the target date and said last week the deal was "98 percent" ready.
But he has also said he will not sign an unsatisfactory agreement and he told Primakov to take a tough line in the sixth round of Russia-NATO talks on the pact.
Yeltsin has said repeatedly that Russia will not back NATO's plans to invite some eastern European countries to join the alliance at a summit in Madrid in July.
But he wants a deal to ensure a peaceful partnership with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation and keep relations with the West on track.

Russia wants a say in NATO decisions and guarantees that the Western defence alliance will not station military structures and nuclear weapons on the territory of ne member states. NATO is reluctant to give such written guarantees.
Primakov indicated before talks started on Tuesday that the deal was not ready and largely depended on Solana's position.
"Let us wait and see what Mr Solana brings," he said.

Some Kremlin sources say Yeltsin has already decided to sign the deal on May 27 but suggest Moscow will keep up the uncertainty and anti-NATO rhetoric until the last minute to appease opponents at home.

Despite Moscow's bitter opposition to NATO enlargement, Russia and the United States agreed on Tuesday to increase defence cooperation in areas ranging from nuclear arms destruction to military reform.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen and Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov signed agreements in Washington to set up joint working groups on anti-missile defence, peacekeeping and post-Soviet reform of Russia's impoverished armed forces.
